newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians set fire to town hall as protest grows.
newsitem.headline: Albanians set fire to town hall as protest grows.

text.p: Angry Albanian protesters on Sunday set fire to the town hall in the southern town of Vlore as a protest over collapsing pyramid investment schemes gathered pace, witnesses said.
Riot police were on alert in the town, 150 km (100 miles) south of the capital Tirana, but witnesses said they seemed reluctant to confront the crowd of about 3,000 people.
The crowd pushed away an army unit standing by but there were no clashes. Eyewitnesses said they had heard explosions, but this could not be confirmed independently.
Last week crowds broke windows of the Vlore town hall as the Gjallica investment scheme, which had offered returns of 11 percent a month, failed to pay them after two weeks of suspended activity.

The protests, which began nearly two weeks ago, have gathered momentum across Albania, with demonstrators all over the Balkan nation taking to the streets, attacking buildings and setting fire to town halls.

The right-wing government of President Sali Berisha has promised to crack down on the pyramid schemes and to return investors' money, but many protesters blame the government for exploiting the schemes for its own gain.
